- Model consistently underestimates prices in early-to-mid forecast horizon (especially 1–7 days ahead), especially during sharp declines or volatility.
- Overestimates prices after recent spikes (e.g., 3–5 days post-peak), suggesting failure to capture mean reversion or momentum decay.
- Tends to overreact to recent high values, leading to exaggerated upward forecasts that later correct.
- Underreacts to sustained downward trends, failing to anticipate sharp drops in the 2–4 day window.
- Forecast mean is often 2–4% below true outcome, indicating persistent downward bias.
- Model exhibits lag in responding to new data, particularly when true values dip sharply after a peak.
- Forecasts show higher variance than actuals, suggesting overconfidence in short-term volatility.
- When history includes a recent high, model often fails to adjust downward sufficiently in the next 3–5 days.
- Model tends to smooth out volatility, underestimating sudden drops or spikes in the 1–3 day horizon.
- Forecasts are more accurate when the 30-day history is trending upward; accuracy drops when history is flat or declining.
